top_story.headline: Rep. Dan Crenshaw still has no 2025 annual financial disclosure on file, 82 days past his final extension
top_story.dek: The Clerk of the House index shows only an extension, filed June 4, 2026, for the Texas Republican.
paragraphs: Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-2) is the only sitting member the Deadline Watch check found with no calendar-year 2025 annual disclosure on file after every extension. He filed for an extension on June 4, 2026. His final extended deadline was August 13, 2026, which is 82 days ago.

The check covers the Clerk of the House index and Senate eFD, but the Senate half failed in this run (a data error on both the annual-report check and the extensions lookup). The finding therefore rests on the House data. A filing under an unexpected spelling of a name can read as missing, so the result is not independently confirmed.

Separately, the Ethics Agreement Tracker lists seven confirmed officials with no posted certification of ethics-agreement compliance, more than 30 days past deadline. The longest overdue is Michelle White Bowman, Federal Reserve Governor and Vice Chairman for Supervision, at 427 days.

sections.eyebrow: Contacts With the President, VP & Cabinet
sections.headline: One DCI Group filing names Secretary of State Marco Rubio next to a West Africa terrorism entry
paragraphs: Of the one FARA filing in the top-officials scan, one has lines that appear to come from a contact log. The OCR interleaves the columns, so the date, method and foreign principal could not be read. No LDA filing named the President or Vice President. The scan is incomplete: 27 recent FARA filings were not read and will be handled in the next run.

items: Secretary of State Marco Rubio (also national security advisor since May 2025): the OCR'd lines of a supplemental statement from DCI Group AZ, LLC (registrant #6278, stamped October 31, 2026) show his name beside the words "partnership to confront terrorism in West Africa" and "Nigeria's National". The method of contact is not stated in the lines, and the foreign principal and date could not be read from them. Filing.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.

The Deadline Watch Senate annual-report check and Senate extensions lookup failed for the same reason, so that check covers the House only. The OGE summary reported one flagged filing, a routine ethics-agreement compliance certification from a Department of State official, and listed no other gaps.
